cases.why: a format holding 2^53: the safe integers bind the whole numbers the list asks for, and a format that is not a string is ignored, so a calendar and the default template prints

cases.name: refuse-month-length-past-the-safe-integers
cases.why: a month's length of 2^53, past the safe integers: not a calendar

cases.name: refuse-year-steps-past-the-safe-integers
cases.why: bundles.year.steps of 2^53, past the safe integers: not a calendar

cases.name: refuse-except-member-past-the-safe-integers
cases.why: an except of [2^53] under every_years 2 (a multiple of it, and larger), past the safe integers: not a calendar

cases.name: refuse-era-start-past-the-safe-integers-written-as-a-float
cases.why: an era's start written 1e300: a whole number however the JSON writes it, and past the safe integers, in a field no year's length adds up: not a calendar

cases.name: unknown-key-in-an-era-holding-a-number-past-the-safe-integers
cases.why: an unknown key inside an era holding 2^53: a reader ignores unknown keys anywhere in the value, so a calendar

cases.name: unknown-key-not-named-x-holding-a-string-past-the-bound
cases.why: an unknown key not named x_, holding a string of 257 characters: a reader ignores unknown keys anywhere in the value, so a calendar

cases.name: refuse-weekday-name-past-the-bound-in-a-week-with-more-names
cases.why: a week of 3 steps with 4 names, the fourth of 257 characters: no weekday prints, and the bound is on the value whether or not a reader prints it: not a calendar

cases.name: refuse-month-name-past-the-bound-by-trailing-spaces
cases.why: a month's name of 250 letters and 7 trailing spaces: 257 characters as decoded, untrimmed: not a calendar

cases.name: refuse-format-past-the-bound-in-version-2
cases.why: a version-2 calendar (a leap rule with an offset) with a format of 257 characters: not a calendar

cases.name: whole-numbers-written-as-floats-in-an-era-and-an-offset
cases.why: an era's start written 0.0 and a leap offset written 1.0: whole numbers however the JSON writes them, so a calendar, read as start 0 and offset 1 (with offset 1, year 3 is the first leap year)

cases.name: months-given-as-zero-reads-as-no-months
cases.why: bundles {"months": 0}: read as no months, like months false (as both the SDK and the Python package read it), so each step is one year

cases.name: months-given-as-an-empty-string-reads-as-no-months
cases.why: bundles {"months": ""}: read as no months, like months false (as both the SDK and the Python package read it), so each step is one year

cases.name: bundles-given-as-false-reads-as-no-months
cases.why: bundles false: read as no months, like months false (as both the SDK and the Python package read it), so each step is one year

cases.name: bundles-given-as-zero-reads-as-no-months
cases.why: bundles 0: read as no months, like months false (as both the SDK and the Python package read it), so each step is one year

cases.name: refuse-week-given-as-false
cases.why: bundles.week given as false: a week that is present and not an object, not a calendar (null is absent; false is not, for a week)

cases.name: year-length-at-the-safe-integers-line
cases.why: two months of 2^52 and 2^52 - 2 days and one day outside them: a year of 2^53 - 1 steps, at the line, a calendar, its dates exact

cases.name: refuse-year-length-past-the-safe-integers
cases.why: two months of 2^52 and 2^52 - 1 days and one day outside them: a year of 2^53 steps, each number inside the line, the sum past it: not a calendar

cases.name: offset-at-the-line-a-date-inside-the-exact-range
cases.why: one month of one day and a leap day every year, offset 2^53 - 1: in year 0 the year index plus the offset is 2^53 - 1, inside the safe integers, so its dates are worded

cases.name: offset-at-the-line-a-date-past-the-exact-range-is-a-plain-number
cases.why: the same calendar: in year 1 the year index plus the offset is 2^53, outside the safe integers, so its dates are plain numbers; the calendar stays a calendar (its year 0 is worded, the case before)

cases.name: era-starting-at-the-line-a-date-whose-year-in-the-era-is-past-it-is-a-plain-number
cases.why: an era starting at -(2^53 - 1) on a year of one step: at its first step the year in the era is 1, worded; at step 0 it is 2^53, outside the safe integers, so that date is a plain number; the calendar stays a calendar

cases.name: step-past-the-exact-range-is-a-plain-number
cases.why: a calendar with neither months nor a year length (each step is one year): the step 2^53 - 1 is worded; the steps 2^53 and -(2^53) are past the safe integers, so plain numbers

cases.name: offset-below-the-line-a-date-past-the-exact-range-is-a-plain-number
cases.why: one month of one day and a leap day every year, offset -(2^53 - 1): in year 0 the year index plus the offset is -(2^53 - 1), inside, worded; in year -1 it is -(2^53), outside, so those dates are plain numbers

cases.name: offset-at-the-line-a-rule-of-every-three-years-a-date-past-it-is-a-plain-number
cases.why: one month of one day and a leap day every 3 years, offset 2^53 - 1: year 0's index plus the offset is 2^53 - 1, inside, worded; year 1's is 2^53, outside, and 2^53 is no leap year of the rule (its remainder by 3 is 2): the date is a plain number whether or not the rule's day falls in it

cases.name: refuse-year-length-past-the-safe-integers-by-a-leap-day
cases.why: two months of 2^52 and 2^52 - 1 days and a leap day every 4 years: the common year is 2^53 - 1, inside, and the longest, every entry counted, 2^53: not a calendar

cases.name: down-era-at-the-line-a-date-whose-year-in-the-era-is-past-it-is-a-plain-number
cases.why: a down era with its pivot at 1 on a year of one step: step -(2^53 - 2) shows year 2^53 - 1, inside, worded; step -(2^53 - 1) shows year 2^53, outside, so a plain number; step 0 shows year 1

cases.name: bundles-given-as-a-string-reads-as-no-bundles
cases.why: bundles "x": not an object, so read as no bundles at all (as both kernels read it), each step one year

cases.name: bundles-given-as-true-reads-as-no-bundles
cases.why: bundles true: not an object, so read as no bundles at all (as both kernels read it), each step one year

cases.name: bundles-given-as-an-empty-list-reads-as-no-bundles
cases.why: bundles []: not an object, so read as no bundles at all (as both kernels read it), each step one year

cases.name: months-given-as-zero-written-as-a-float-reads-as-no-months
cases.why: bundles.months 0.0: 0 however written, read as no months, each step one year

cases.name: refuse-months-given-as-true
cases.why: bundles.months true: not an object with its names and lengths, and not false, 0 or an empty string: not a calendar

cases.name: refuse-months-given-as-an-empty-list
cases.why: bundles.months []: not an object with its names and lengths, and not false, 0 or an empty string: not a calendar

cases.name: year-given-as-null-reads-as-no-year
cases.why: bundles.year null: absent, so neither months nor a year length, each step one year

cases.name: refuse-year-given-as-false
cases.why: bundles.year false on a calendar without months: present and not an object holding its steps, not a calendar (only months, bundles and null read as absent)

cases.name: refuse-year-given-as-zero
cases.why: bundles.year 0 on a calendar without months: present and not an object holding its steps, not a calendar (only months, bundles and null read as absent)

cases.name: refuse-year-given-as-an-empty-string
cases.why: bundles.year "" on a calendar without months: present and not an object holding its steps, not a calendar (only months, bundles and null read as absent)

cases.name: refuse-year-given-as-an-empty-object
cases.why: bundles.year {} on a calendar without months: present and not an object holding its steps, not a calendar (only months, bundles and null read as absent)

cases.name: refuse-year-given-as-false-beside-good-months
cases.why: bundles.year false beside good months: the months win only over a year that is an object holding its steps; this one is not, so not a calendar

cases.name: refuse-year-given-as-an-empty-object-beside-good-months
cases.why: bundles.year {} beside good months: the months win only over a year that is an object holding its steps; this one is not, so not a calendar

cases.name: refuse-week-given-as-an-empty-object
cases.why: bundles.week {} beside good months: an object without its length, not a calendar

cases.name: refuse-year-length-past-the-safe-integers-by-leap-days-never-in-one-year
cases.why: two months of 2^52 and 2^52 - 2 days and two leap days every 2 years, offsets 0 and 1, so never in one year: the longest year that occurs is 2^53 - 1, but every entry counted is 2^53: not a calendar

cases.name: offset-at-the-line-on-the-second-leap-rule-a-date-past-it-is-a-plain-number
cases.why: one month of one day and two leap days every year, offsets 1 and 2^53 - 1: in year 0 both sums are inside, worded; in year 1 the first rule's is 2, the second's 2^53, outside, so the date is a plain number: each leap rule's offset counts, not the first rule's alone

cases.name: v1-ignores-a-malformed-except-and-an-offset-past-the-safe-integers
cases.why: a version-1 value whose leap entry carries except "x" and offset 2^60: on version 1 both are unknown keys, not read and not checked, so a calendar worded as the plain rule (every 4 from index 0)

cases.name: v1-ignores-an-offset-at-the-line-a-date-a-version-2-reading-makes-plain-is-worded
cases.why: a version-1 rule of every year carrying offset 2^53 - 1: on version 1 the offset is an unknown key, so year 1 (steps 2 and 3), which a version-2 reading would make a plain number, is worded

cases.name: refuse-week-without-names
cases.why: a week of 7 steps with no names beside good months: bundles.week.names is not a list of strings, not a calendar

cases.name: refuse-year-steps-zero-beside-good-months
cases.why: bundles.year.steps 0 beside good months: not a whole number from 1, so not a calendar, though the months win over a good year

cases.name: refuse-year-steps-null-beside-good-months
cases.why: bundles.year.steps null beside good months: not a whole number from 1, so not a calendar, though the months win over a good year

cases.name: offset-below-the-line-on-the-first-of-two-leap-rules-a-date-past-it-is-a-plain-number
cases.why: one month of one step and two leap days every year, offsets -(2^53 - 1) then 0: in year 0 both sums are inside, worded; in year -1 the first rule's is -(2^53), outside, so step -1 is a plain number: not only the last rule, and not only the largest offset, counts

cases.name: v1-ignores-an-except-past-the-bound-and-an-offset-with-no-every-years
cases.why: a version-1 value whose day outside the months has no every_years, an offset of 1 and an except of nine members: on version 1 both are unknown keys, so neither the except's bound nor the offset's need of every_years is asked, and the day falls in every year
